seo_description: Free, open-source macOS menu bar app. Press Option+Space, fill in a small form of variables, and paste finished text. No account, no server, no network.
hero_sub: Press Option+Space to open a floating palette, pick a template, fill in its fields, and paste the finished text into the app you were using.
features_sub: Customer replies, meeting notes, and commit messages get a form instead of find-and-replace.

features.title: Global hotkey palette
features.desc: Option+Space opens a centered floating panel with a searchable list sorted by recent use. The hotkey can be re-recorded in Settings.

features.title: Typed placeholders
features.desc: Write {{name}}, defaults, multi-line text, dates with day offsets, or choice lists. Each placeholder becomes the right input, with a live preview beside it.

features.title: Paste or copy
features.desc: Command+Return pastes into the previous app and Option+Return only copies. You can optionally restore your original clipboard afterward.

features.title: Built-in variables
features.desc: Use {{@date}}, {{@date(-1)}}, {{@time}}, and {{@clipboard}} without typing anything. Date and time formats are configurable.

features.title: Template manager
features.desc: Edit titles, tags, and bodies, insert placeholders from a menu, and check a parse report that flags unclosed braces or empty choices.

features.title: Local and private
features.desc: Templates live in a JSON file on your Mac, with import and export. There is no account, server, or network access.

permissions_step: To let the app paste for you, grant Accessibility access in System Settings > Privacy & Security > Accessibility; without it, text is copied to the clipboard instead.

faq.q: Is SnippetFormPalette free and open source?
faq.a: Yes. It is free to use and released under the MIT license, and the full source is on GitHub. If it saves you time, there is an optional Support button in the app.

Templates are saved as JSON at ~/Library/Application Support/SnippetFormPalette/templates.json, and settings are kept in UserDefaults. Nothing is sent anywhere, and you can export your templates to a JSON file at any time.
Notarization requires a paid Apple Developer account, and this is a free open-source project. Right-click the app and choose Open once to launch it, or build it yourself from source with Xcode.
